newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $63 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $63 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales near midday Friday were light at $63.00 per cwt, unchanged from this week's activity, feedlot sources said.
About 400 slaughter steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas following a weekly movement of 90,100 head, the sources said.
No sales were reported in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area after weekly volume of 93,400 head.
Bids were scattered at $63.00 per cwt and being passed by most owners who priced cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, they said.
The lack of significant carryover supplies and quick pickups of cattle sold late this week stimulated bullish outlooks for fed cattle prices next week, sources said.
Fed cattle prices next week could firm to $64.00, provided packer demand remains strong and there are no surprises in this afternoon's USDA monthly cattle report, they said.

Friday's report was expected to show on-feed supplies as of June 1 at 113.2 percent of a year ago in the seven key states, according to the average of analysts' pre-report estimates. May placements were seen at 117.2 percent and May marketings at 99.0 percent.
